sara: FYI — discovered KMS-wrapped blobs in partner-ingest logs that were unwrapped by partner-ingest-sa yesterday. Looks like some old backup artifacts were rehydrated during a retry job. Need an urgent rotation + RBAC sweep.

josh: can you paste the exact log line and which ciphertext/key id?

sara: log snippet:
```
2025-09-12T22:14:02Z partner-ingest ERROR unseal: unwrapped_ciphertext=ciC1...abc key_id=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/partner-enc-1 principal=serviceAccount:partner-ingest-sa@partners.gserviceaccount.com
```

mira: ugh. That key is customer-partitioned -> backed by our KMS key. If partner-ingest-sa had IAM to decrypt, we need to know scope: was it the least-priv binding or a broad grant?

josh: checking IAM now. @devops-bot can you dump iam bindings for that key and recent access logs?

devops-bot: scheduled job kicked off: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy partner-enc-1 --location global --keyring ingest` and `gcloud logging read "resource.type=kms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName=google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign" --freshness=72h` — results in #ops-alert in 3m.

dan-oncall: while we wait — propose immediate mitigations: 1) create a rotated key pair and rewrap all active ciphertexts in partner cluster, 2) revoke the long-lived IAM binding from partner-ingest-sa, 3) enable an audit-only deny on broad decrypts for 4h to block new unwraps. Thoughts? :warning:

josh: agree. also list affected buckets/objects and run a targeted blob rewrap. We should avoid a full mass re-encrypt unless we confirm exposure.

sara: Quick inventory I ran: 5 buckets in staging/partnerA (older backups), 2 archived objects in prod-partnerA-backups with matching ciphertext prefix. I can kick off a rewrap job for staging canary.

mira: RBAC change: move partner-ingest-sa from roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to a scoped custom role with condition `resource.name.startsWith("projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/partnerA-")` — that reduces blast radius. I'll open the PR.

josh: also add a Vault transit rewrap step. For Vault (transit) we used wrapped KMS keys for wrapping. Command to rewrap in Vault: 
```bash
# rewrap all ciphertext keys in path transit/enc
vault write -f transit/rewrap
```
Keep a canary: run for path `transit/keys/partnerA-backups` first.

dan-oncall: timeline proposal: canary rewrap starts in 30m, monitor 1h, then broader rewrap overnight. RBAC revoke immediately (within 15m). Audit-only deny for 4h while we validate.

sara: I'll start the canary and post progress. Also adding the object list to the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4782

mira: I'll attach the IAM diff in the PR and add a fallback plan to restore the previous binding if something breaks. Add diagnostic flags: `--dry-run` for iam apply and label changes as `sec:rot2025`.

josh: keep an eye on KMS audit logs for any unusual decrypts after revoke. If we still see decrypt activity, escalate to cloud provider support.

devops-bot: iam dump finished. Bindings show partner-ingest-sa had `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` at keyRing level (too broad). Last decrypt entries: 2025-09-12T22:14 & 22:19 from that SA. Dump link: gs://redwood-ops-dumps/1751234560/kms-iam.txt

sara: canary rewrap kicked off at 1751234740. command: `python tools/rewraper.py --prefix partnerA --mode canary`

josh: good. add a health-check: after rewrap, try a rehydrate using the new key w/ partner test principal. Make sure logs match `rewrap-ok` tag.

mira: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821 — includes conditional role and terraform plan. Please review and approve fast.

dan-oncall: I'm going to apply immediate revoke: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding partner-enc-1 --member=serviceAccount:partner-ingest-sa@partners.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` — will run at 1751234880. Expect 1-2min propagation.

sara: revoke done. Confirmed no new decrypt events for 10m in logs. Can we set a temporary allow list for partner's ingest job using short-lived tokens instead?

josh: yes — shift them to a signed JWT flow that only allows decrypt via our proxy service which enforces context checks. Long-term: remove direct KMS access for partner SAs.

mira: put a note in the runbook: ensure `audit_configs` for KMS are set to include DATA_ACCESS logging for the key and sink logs to our secure bucket. Also add log-based alert for any decrypt from non-whitelisted principals.

devops-bot: canary rewrap reported 12 objects rewrapped, 0 failures, started 1751234740 ended 1751234825 — logs: gs://redwood-ops-dumps/1751234560/rewrap-canary.log

sara: moving to broader rewrap tonight at 02:00 UTC with a short maintenance window. I'll coordinate with partner ops for read-only freeze.

josh: assign owners: rewrap owner = sara, RBAC PR owner = mira, monitoring + alerting = josh, escalation = dan-oncall.

mira: added postmortem checklist item to verify rotation across dedicated clusters and to run a scanning job for any leaked plaintext snapshots.

dan-oncall: closing immediate containment. follow-up items: rotate KMS key (create new key version and revoke older versions), sweep service accounts for overly broad KMS roles, and schedule a compliance audit. I'll file follow-ups in SEC-4782. :white_check_mark:

sara: thanks team. will post status updates to #incident-response and update ticket.

josh: small note — we should consider short TTL ephemeral wrapped tokens for partners (15m) and require re-auth for large restores. Saves us from rewrap churn.

mira: agreed. adding as roadmap item for secrets-hardening epic.

sara: end-of-thread status: canary success, revoke applied, broader run scheduled. will update after global rewrap completes. :lock:
